analysis:
Examined the head text of QwenTensorParallelNativeBatchExecutor.swift and the Batch.swift patch plus base text. The PR adds a default-off buildsAhead flag (executor init, line 104), splits select() into buildSelection and readSelection (lines 460-582), and adds submitDecode/readDecode (lines 598-635). The resident runtime passes batchBuildsAhead to both executor and driver (Batch.swift head lines 232/234). The flag is defined elsewhere, so the default is not verifiable here.

Security-relevant observations:
- Build-ahead checks: submitDecode requires buildsAhead, distinct lanes, no assistant, and an empty accepted queue. For .after, the prior step's lanes must be identical objects. Token IDs are range-checked. readSelection keeps the same validation (finite logits, token range, control word length and finiteness) and advances sampler history only after all checks pass on rank 0. This matches the earlier read-then-build behavior and is not a regression.
- Sampler state: logprobs are captured per step (line 530). The sampler draw happens at build time, before the read. If an earlier submitted step fails, the sampler state or penalty history may already have advanced, but the whole batch fails (control.fail in the Batch.swift catch), so no cross-request leakage appears.
- Prefix-cache and SSD persist paths (T-041) are unchanged. confirmedRetirement still requires a clean retirement and a closed lane, and the HMAC scoping and tenant scope derivation are untouched. Build-ahead lanes bypass nothing in the capture or persist logic, since the lane state flow is unchanged.
- Availability (T-010, A-018): selectedCount is incremented at submit time (line 627). retire() verifies selected <= lane.selectedCount and computes discardedDecodeForwards from it. This is consistent for unread submitted steps, but the driver (not supplied) must drain or discard them. Cancellation and drain interactions with the driver's serveAhead are unverified.
- Cross-rank agreement on buildsAhead: the comment on cohortJoinsAhead says both ranks must agree. The same holds for buildsAhead, and the sealed-group or load-agreement binding for it is outside the supplied evidence.

No concrete regression is identified. Remaining questions: QwenTensorParallelBatchDriver build-ahead logic, QwenTensorParallelBatchSession.submitDecode, and where batchBuildsAhead is set.
